instruction: I'd like to explore the academic backgrounds of the authors from UT Austin and SJTU who contributed to this paper. Please find their personal webpages and save them to a bookmark folder named 'Liked Authors' in the 'Bookmarks bar'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-20)

metadata.explanation: Task focuses on authors from UT Austin (Yuke Zhu) and SJTU (Haoyi Zhu). Expected URLs based on institutional affiliations and typical academic profiles. Uses existing bookmark evaluator.

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly verifies all three requirements: finding author webpages, saving to 'Liked Authors' folder, and placing in the Bookmarks bar
The getter (get_bookmarks) successfully extracts bookmark state from Chrome's persistent storage without requiring postconfig
The metric logic correctly handles multiple possible URLs per author using combination matching (product(*urls))
Expected URLs are semantically appropriate for the identified authors (Yuke Zhu from UT Austin with 5 possible URLs, Haoyi Zhu from SJTU with 1 URL)
The evaluation logic at chrome.py:176-200 properly searches for the 'Liked Authors' folder and validates URL contents
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The exact set match requirement (line 196: set(combination) == set(liked_authors_urls)) may be overly strict - it will fail if the agent bookmarks additional relevant pages while 'exploring academic backgrounds', though this strictness does align with the specific instruction to bookmark only UT Austin and SJTU authors
